clue.text: Mineral covered in chemical

indicators.note: the answer sits covered by the letters of the next word, enclosed within it

explanation.surface: A mineral coated in some chemical substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' points to the run of letters inside 'chemical': cheMICAl.
explanation.definitionFit: Mica is a silicate mineral that splits into thin glassy sheets.

clue.text: Take time out of thinking for shuttle diplomacy?

indicators.note: with 'out of', this asks for one letter to be removed from the word that follows
with 'Take', this says the time letter is removed from the thinking word

parts.note: meditation is deep thinking or contemplation

explanation.surface: A suggestion to pause one's thinking, framed as a description of diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take ... out of' removes a T from MEDITATION. The question mark flags that shuttle diplomacy is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shuttle diplomacy is a go-between carrying messages between parties, a form of brokering a settlement.

clue.text: Possibly London's assets

definitions.meaning: London is an example of a country's chief city, hence 'Possibly'
money and property held by a business

explanation.surface: A remark about the wealth belonging to London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London's' reads as a possessive, but it is 'London is': London is (possibly) a capital, here an example of a seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: London is a chief city of a country, and a firm's assets or funds are also called by this financial word.

clue.text: Catch nothing about abstract style

indicators.note: turned about, so the catch and the nothing together are read from right to left

parts.note: a trap is a device for catching
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: Someone reaching for a catch and coming up empty, set beside an art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TRAPO back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s movement of abstract painting using optical illusions.

clue.text: Withdrawing from local authority work, having time at home with illness

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
someone at home is in
gout is a painful illness of the joints

explanation.surface: Someone stays home sick, taking time off work.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain in the 1990s, schools could leave local council control, a move called by this phrase. 'having', 'at' and 'with' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Choosing to leave a scheme or authority's control is a voluntary departure from it.

clue.text: Perpetual sage is this when only his head remains!

parts.words: sage is this when only his head remains
parts.note: the word sage keeps only its first letter when the three letters spelling time are dropped, so it is sage without its age

explanation.surface: A joke about a wise man reduced to just a head.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AGE away from SAGE and only S, its head, is left: the sage is then 'age-less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perpetual never grows old, so time leaves no mark on it.

clue.text: Amount left to volunteers to begin with

indicators.note: the first two pieces are placed at the start, before the letter for left

parts.note: taken as written
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve army

explanation.surface: Money left to a volunteer group in a will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to begin with' puts the first two pieces ahead of the letter for left. The Territorial Army is Britain's reserve of part-time volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the whole sum or quantity reached by adding up.

clue.text: Country loses a bit jutting out

indicators.note: the country gives up a letter, which is removed from its name

parts.note: China is a country in East Asia

explanation.surface: A nation forfeits a small protruding piece of territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes the A off CHINA.
explanation.definitionFit: The chin is the part of the face that projects below the mouth.

clue.text: Holy types church sets free without hesitation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the hesitation sound is left out of the word for sets free

parts.note: liberates means releases or sets free
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A church releases its clergy, and does so promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' leaves LIBATES once the hesitation is gone; the Church of England's abbreviation goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Celibates are people who abstain from marriage, often clergy or monks under religious vows.

clue.text: Influence in part of church

parts.note: taken as written
a spire is the tall pointed tower of a church

explanation.surface: Power held within one section of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire someone is to stir or move them, shaping what they do.

clue.text: Present-date mail sorted and put into separate pigeon-holes?

indicators.note: the letters are sorted into a new order, as mail is sorted

explanation.surface: Today's post is sorted and filed in the right slots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted' rearranges the fifteen letters of PRESENTDATEMAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To departmentalise is to divide into separate sections, figuratively boxing things off.

clue.text: First part of play about war?

parts.note: Act I is the opening act of a play
on can mean about, as in a talk on a topic

explanation.surface: The opening of a drama concerned with a war.
explanation.walkthrough: ACT I is written with the Roman numeral I. The question mark marks war as an example of fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Military action means fighting in battle, which a war consists of.

clue.text: From the library of former learner, one book sir wanted back

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word sir is wanted the wrong way round, read backwards

explanation.surface: An ex-student had a book, and the master wants it returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SIR into RIS. 'wanted' only links. The Latin phrase is printed on bookplates.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase on a bookplate names the owner of the volume.

clue.text: What in short would appear to be sick state

definitions.text: What in short would appear to be sick state

parts.words: What in short would appear to be sick state
parts.note: a US state whose standard short form reads like an everyday word for unwell

explanation.surface: A riddle about a place whose abbreviation suggests poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: The state's abbreviation is ILL., which looks like the word for sick.
explanation.definitionFit: This Midwestern US state is abbreviated Ill., a word meaning unwell.

clue.text: Lager nine gets drunk usually

indicators.note: a drunk person's words come out jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Nine pints of lager and someone is usually drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets drunk' rearranges the letters of LAGERNINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true as a rule holds for most cases, as normally does.

clue.text: Wild cat — that's first demolished bit of plant

indicators.note: the opening letter of the big cat is knocked off

parts.note: a panther is a large wild cat, a leopard

explanation.surface: A big cat flattens part of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first demolished' removes P, the first letter of PANTHER. 'that's' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The anther is the pollen-bearing tip of a flower's stamen.

clue.text: Hopeless state of protest when leader's been replaced

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for protest is swapped for another

parts.note: an objection is a protest

explanation.surface: A deposed leader leaves a protest movement in despair.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading O of OBJECTION is replaced by A. Which letter comes in is left for the solver to find from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Abjection is utter wretchedness, a condition of misery and degradation.

clue.text: Funny Eurocrat enthralling any number as anecdotist

indicators.note: holds the number captive within the rearranged letters
funny here means odd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: An amusing EU official captivates a crowd with stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges EUROCRAT into RACOTEUR, and 'enthralling' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of stories.

clue.text: Figure of love

definitions.meaning: a numeral, here the digit zero
the score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: A phrase that sounds like a portrait or statue of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, love means a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is a numeral, and love is the zero score in tennis.

clue.text: Tour going wrong — time to expose scandal

indicators.note: the letters of tour go wrong, falling into a new order

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A tour goes badly and it is time to reveal the scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' rearranges TOUR into OUTR; 'to expose' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal provokes public indignation and shock.

clue.text: Splendid joke I fed into Scotsman

indicators.note: the joke and the I are put inside the Scotsman

parts.note: Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A man feeds a joke into a Scottish newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed into' signals the container. Mac is a familiar, rather old-fashioned name for any Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means grand and impressive, having stately dignity.

clue.text: Fellow starting new deal as a statesman

indicators.note: the fellow comes at the start of the answer

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: the letters of deal are made new by being rearranged

explanation.surface: A man launching a new deal as a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DEAL into DEL. 'as' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Mandela was South Africa's first black president, a famous political leader.

clue.text: Growth as high as it could be

definitions.text: Growth as high as it could be

parts.words: Growth as high as it could be
parts.note: hair growing on the very top of the head, tied up there

explanation.surface: A plant or tumour growing as tall as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' suggests a plant, but it is hair tied up at the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is hair gathered into a bun or tuft on the crown of the head.

clue.text: Special perfomer to astound brown, male brought in

parts.note: to stun is to astound

indicators.note: the male letter is brought inside the colour word

parts.note: tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: A performer amazes a man with a tan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' signals the container; 'to' only links. 'perfomer' is the clue's misspelling of performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuntman performs dangerous action sequences in films, a specialist doubling for the actor.

clue.text: You can have them out — in the home also!

indicators.note: the answer is found lying in the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something you can enjoy away or under your own roof too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters inside hoME ALSo.
explanation.definitionFit: People eat lunch or dinner out at restaurants as well as at home.

clue.text: Pianist in clubs havin' aspirations

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
having aspirations means hoping, spelt with the final letter dropped as the clue's dropped g shows

explanation.surface: A piano player at a club, chatting about his hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'havin'' shows the -g is dropped, so 'hoping' becomes HOPIN'. 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Chopin was a Polish Romantic composer and celebrated concert pianist.

clue.text: Permission needed to go ahead with the match

definitions.text: Permission needed to go ahead with the match

parts.words: Permission needed to go ahead with the match
parts.note: the match is a wedding, not a sporting fixture, and the permission is a legal document allowing it

explanation.surface: Approval required before a sports fixture can be played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the match' looks like a game, but it is a union of two people.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal document authorising a couple to wed.

clue.text: Consider what's to be paid (pounds)

parts.note: a fee is a charge to be paid
L stands for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Thinking over the bill in pounds sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel can mean to believe or hold an opinion.

clue.text: Wicked activity round American city gets one killed

indicators.note: the word for wicked activity goes round the city

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Crime around a US city gets someone murdered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the container; 'gets one' only links, leaving 'killed' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slain means murdered, put to death violently.

clue.text: Agitation said to finish off Leicester!

indicators.note: the ending of the city's name is spoken, giving a sound for the answer

parts.note: Leicester is pronounced Lester, so its last syllable sounds like ster

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to finish off Leicester's sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester, an English city, is said 'Lester', so its ending sounds 'ster'. 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a commotion or disturbance.
